name: harness-selftest
description: harness self-verification -- real devices, real corners, no design claim
claim: harness self-verification -- proves sim/harness (#2) resolves the PDK, sweeps the repo's PVT corner grid, and writes a sim/README.md-conformant evidence record end to end. Not a design or spec claim for any block.
methodology: idsat_n / idsat_p: diode-connected nfet_03v3 / pfet_03v3 (W=2um L=0.28um) drive current, read as the DC-settled average of a single .tran analysis (avg i(...) from=10n to=190n, well before the resistor step below) -- mirrors sim/devchar-delay's dc_idn/dc_idp convention.

res_tau: raw .measure trig/targ on the step response of a ppolyf_u resistor (W=1um L=10um) into a 1 pF load, from the input step's 10% crossing to the output's 63.2% crossing (one RC time constant) -- exercises the harness's raw_measures (.measure) pass-through mechanism against real ngspice output, not just a unit-tested string composition.

Simulator settings: single .tran 1n 1u analysis (1 ns print interval, adaptive internal timestep); no statistical switches touched (design.ngspice defaults: sw_stat_global = sw_stat_mismatch = 0, nominal skew only).

This experiment is deliberately architecture-agnostic infrastructure: it exists to prove the harness itself, not to characterize a PLL block. sim/devchar-delay / sim/devchar-cp / sim/devchar-passives remain the real device-characterization evidence for #8/#9/#10.

res_tau.expr: trig v(rin) val='0.1*vdd_val' rise=1 targ v(n_out) val='0.632*vdd_val' rise=1
